## Validation and limitations

Nine screened relevant records were retrieved: **9/9, or 100% relative recall against the development set**. This is not an independent validation result or absolute sensitivity; no user seeds, independent benchmark, or held-out set were available.

The long-term follow-up block was tested and left out. It reduced the count to 10,190 (58.4%), but only nine known records were available, below the skill’s threshold for requiring an optional block. The loss sample found 0/30 clearly eligible records, which is too small to establish safety. Follow-up timing remains for screening. Even with that block, retrieval would exceed the 10,000-record standard workload budget.

I assumed “anxiety-related disorders” includes OCD and PTSD as well as anxiety disorders; confirm that scope and the minimum follow-up interval for “long-term.” The counts use the current PubMed index constrained by Entrez date, not a reconstruction of the exact 2017 interface or indexing state.

The draft needs PRESS peer review by an information specialist before use.
